$comment: CAP: 12 prose entries across expected_shape · read_this_way · suspicious_if ·
blind_spots · decisions · review_notes · expected · known_normal · known_bad ·
do_not_reflag · how_to_investigate · limitations. This file carries 10, and
descriptor.interpretation.entries must equal that number. There are exactly two
legal resolutions when a 13th wants in: PROMOTE it to a check, or DELETE it.
There is no overflow file and no overflow block.
`fences` and `counts` are RECORD blocks, not prose — they are not counted against
the cap. `fences` lives here because the descriptor schema's root is
additionalProperties:false and has no fences category (Spec 120 §14.0).

expected_shape.what: A healthy run reports one observation per SELECTED check and nothing else; the audit table therefore has exactly as many rows as the chain selects — permits 3, coa 2, sources 6, standalone 9.

read_this_way.what: Every row value is a VIOLATION COUNT against `viol == 0`, not a population. `permit_columns: 0` means zero expected columns were missing, not that zero columns were checked; the population lives in the check's `expect` array.

suspicious_if.signal: permit_cost_type_sample reports 0 violations on a run where the CKAN datastore was unreachable — the check returns true on a non-OK sample response, so 'verified' and 'never ran' are the same row.

A sources run completes in under a second. The step issues 18 network requests on the sources chain with no timeout and no retry; sub-second completion means something answered from a cache or a proxy, not that the archives are reachable.

blind_spots.what: The five archive checks are HTTP HEAD only. A reachable ZIP whose .dbf attributes have drifted passes this step and fails later, inside the loader that downloads it.

The zoning pre-flight asserts the upsert key and geometry (plus HT_LABEL and PRCNT_CVER on the two overlays that carry them) and nothing else; the remaining attribute drift is only caught at load time by zoning-attr-drift.js.

Nothing here observes a process kill. The ledger strand window closes THROWN errors only; a SIGKILL, an OOM or a runner cancel inside the 21-request network window leaves the pipeline_runs row 'running' and no check can see it.

measured.value: 0 checks cover process death; the window is a `finally`

decisions.what: permit_cost_type_sample is declared blocking:true, matching what the code does today, rather than the draft's blocking:false.
decisions.why: A non-blocking FAIL is invisible to /api/quality (run-chain writes the literal status 'completed'), and the review followup requires that to be resolved BEFORE any pilot declares one. Declaring blocking:false would also have smuggled a real behaviour change into a commit whose whole claim is that it changes nothing.

decisions.what: The four fences are carried in the OPEN — descriptor fields and one declared check — never hidden inside compute.
decisions.why: 58914fa8 becomes zoning_resource_columns.expect.resources; 1ceebd17 and f6047e89 become inputs.reads.externals entries and subjects of source_archives_reachable; 646ea5a7 becomes its own declared check, address_point_coordinate_source, whose OR-rule is stated in the check's why and in limitations because no limit form can express it.

known_normal.what: parcel_columns reporting 0 violations on the permits and coa chains is normal and is NOT evidence the parcels CSV was fetched. The source block is chain-gated, so on those two chains the compute reports a constant zero — exactly what the pre-conversion step did with its parcels_schema_mismatch_count rows.

fences.const: hasCoordinateSource() over the Address Points header, with LATITUDE/LONGITUDE/geometry kept OUT of the flat expect list
fences.incident: WF3 2026-05-30 — the flat LATITUDE/LONGITUDE requirement was dead on arrival: the live CSV ships a geometry GeoJSON column, so the flat form false-failed while the real loss mode (no coordinate source at all → a 0-row spatial bridge) went unchecked.

fences.const: ZONING_RESOURCES — 10 CKAN DataStore resource ids with THREE distinct required column sets
fences.value: base 6 (_id, geometry, ZN_ZONE, ZN_STRING, COVERAGE, FSI_TOTAL) · height overlay adds HT_LABEL · lot-coverage overlay adds PRCNT_CVER · seven overlays require _id + geometry only
fences.incident: Spec 58 zoning enrichment — CRITICAL+HIGH: an overlay silently dropped from the pre-flight set, or a required attribute collapsed to the generic overlay pair, lets a zoning load run against a resource that no longer carries the column the enricher reads.

Spec 59 §8c — datastore_active=false for the ravine layer, so reachability is the ONLY pre-flight signal; without it a vanished archive is first noticed by load-ravines.js after the chain has already started writing.

Spec 62 §8c — same class as the ravine fence: the 40-column attribute and FEATURE_CODE_DESC/JURISDICTION value checks only run post-download, so losing the reachability HEAD removes every pre-flight signal the centreline load has.
